It faced many lawsuits and withdrew the device from the US market in 1986 citing litigation costs, but the company itself continued to operate and was later acquired by Monsanto and then Pfizer. Stating both went bankrupt is false.

claims.quote: Use of the pill has dropped by nearly a half in the last two decades

claims.quote: It has been associated with huge increases in infertility
claims.evidence: Medical consensus confirms that oral contraceptives do not cause infertility. Fertility typically returns to normal shortly after discontinuing use. This claim is false.

claims.quote: It has been associated with huge increases in... ectopic pregnancy
claims.evidence: This is misleading. Oral contraceptives significantly reduce the overall risk of ectopic pregnancy by preventing pregnancy. The claim omits this primary protective effect and focuses only on the increased *conditional* risk if the method fails. This decontextualization is a disinformation tactic. Source: PLOS One (2014), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0115031.

claims.quote: It has been associated with huge increases in... breast and cervical cancer
claims.evidence: This is an exaggeration and misleading by omission. While there is a small, documented increase in risk for breast and cervical cancers, the claim of 'huge increases' is false. Critically, the speaker omits the fact that oral contraceptives are proven to significantly DECREASE the risk of ovarian, endometrial, and colorectal cancers. Source: National Cancer Institute.

claims.quote: It has been associated with huge increases in... pelvic inflammatory disease
claims.evidence: This claim is false. Medical literature suggests that combination oral contraceptives have a protective effect, reducing the risk of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID). The claim directly contradicts scientific evidence.

claims.quote: It has been associated with huge increases in... endometrial atrophy
claims.evidence: This is misleading. Endometrial atrophy (thinning of the lining) is a known and often intended physiological effect of hormonal contraceptives, which leads to lighter periods. Framing this as a 'huge increase' in a 'serious condition' alongside cancer is deceptive.

title.english: False Claims About Contraceptive Pill Failure Rates and Health Risks
title.spanish: Afirmaciones Falsas Sobre las Tasas de Fallo de las Píldoras Anticonceptivas y Riesgos para la Salud

claims.quote: There's... an 80 to 90% chance of failure [for contraceptive pills] over a 10-year period.
claims.evidence: This is a gross exaggeration. Medical Daily (https://www.medicaldaily.com/effectiveness-rates-hormonal-pills-oral-contraceptives-common-birth-control-side-effects-475046) reports a typical use failure rate of 9% per year. The correct cumulative probability of failure over 10 years is approximately 61.1% (1 - 0.91^10), not 80-90%.

claims.quote: There's roughly a 40 to 50% chance of failure over a period of five years
claims.evidence: This is false. The cumulative probability of failure over 5 years with a 9% annual typical use failure rate (per Medical Daily) is approximately 37.6% (1 - 0.91^5), which is below the claimed 40-50% range.

claims.quote: the manufacturers of IUDs, A. H. Robins, G. D. Searle company, have been sued so often, they're bankrupt.
claims.evidence: This is partially false and misleading. A.H. Robins did file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 1985 due to lawsuits over the Dalkon Shield IUD (Source: Wikipedia). However, G.D. Searle, maker of the Copper-7 IUD, did not go bankrupt; it was acquired by Monsanto in 1985 and later by Pfizer (Source: CNN). The claim that both manufacturers are bankrupt is false.

claims.quote: Use of the pill... has been associated with huge increases in infertility
claims.evidence: This contradicts the established medical consensus. According to Medical Daily (https://www.medicaldaily.com/are-birth-control-pills-safe-long-term-what-know-about-birth-control-pill-risks-474935), "Long-term pill use does not permanently damage fertility. Most people resume ovulation within weeks to a few months after stopping, and many conceive within a year if no other fertility problems exist."

claims.quote: current methods of natural means to responsible Parenthood are every bit as effective as any pills or chemicals you might use, 98% method effective and 94% user effective.
claims.evidence: This is a misleading oversimplification. While the 98% 'method effective' (perfect use) rate is plausible for some specific methods, the 94% 'user effective' (typical use) rate is an exaggeration. According to the CDC and other medical sources, the typical use effectiveness for fertility awareness-based methods has a wide range of 77-98%, making the typical failure rate much higher than implied and generally less effective than hormonal pills (~93% typical effectiveness).

claims.quote: They cost nothing
claims.evidence: This is misleading. While there is no recurring cost for a prescription, effective use of these methods often requires initial training, classes, charting tools, apps, or devices like a basal body thermometer, all of which can have associated costs.
